newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine interest rates won't stay high-de Ocamp.
newsitem.headline: Philippine interest rates won't stay high-de Ocamp.

text.p: High Philippine interest rates, used to defend the peso, will not stay that way for long, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo told Reuters on Wednesday.
"This is just a short-term phenomenon. We don't expect it to last a long time," he said.
Interest rates are at their highest since the Mexico peso crisis hit the Philippine economy eary in 1995.

The central bank, which gave in last week to speculative attacks and allowed an 11.5 percent plunge in the peso, said on Tuesday it would hang on to a tight monetary policy until the market calmed down.
De Ocampo said it was too early to say whether the government would revise its borrowing programme because of the high local interest rates.
The 91-day Treasury bill rate hit a two-year high on Monday of 13.217 percent.
"We're happy that our interest structure has been much better because we have been able to float long-term bonds in the past," he said.
Earlier this year, the Philippines became the first country in the region to issue a 20-year Treasury bond.

"I tend to think the period of adjustment will not be too long. In the end we will see the peso seeking its own proper level which may not be as drastic as some speculators think it will be," De Ocampo said.
